paragraphs.text: Shipment MZN-10-06 occurred at Manzanillo on 2010-05-13. A former laboratory worker now in contact with the reporting office described a northbound load of agricultural chemicals leaving the Manzanillo terminal that the source initially believed to be precursor material. On closer questioning the source conceded that the load had cleared inspection with full documentation and that the consignee was a fertilizer distributor with no known connection to any trafficking network. The reporting office includes the account because the source raised it unprompted and because it illustrates the difficulty of distinguishing legitimate chemical traffic from diversion at this terminal.

The source described the general pattern of chemical imports through the port during the spring as heavy, with several consignments a week arriving for the agricultural and mining sectors. The source stated that yard staff do not inspect sealed drums as a matter of routine and that documentation is accepted at face value when the importer is known. The source had no information suggesting that this particular consignee was diverting material, and the reporting office has no other reporting on the firm.

The reporting office assesses this as background reporting on terminal practice rather than as information on a specific network. The source's access to the terminal is historical and the source now relies on former colleagues for current information. Readers should treat the account as a description of how legitimate and illegitimate chemical traffic can look alike at the point of entry. No operational tasking should be based on this reporting without further validation.
